abstract: The paper provides a quantitative examination of the link between political institutions and deaths during the first 100 days of the COVID-19 pandemic. The study demonstrates that countries with more democratic political institutions experienced deaths on a larger per capita scale than less democratic countries, with results robust to the inclusion of many relevant controls, a battery of estimation techniques, and estimation with instruments for the institutional measures. Additionally, the authors examine the extent to which COVID-19 deaths were impacted heterogeneously by policy responses across types of political institutions, finding that policy responses in democracies were less effective in reducing deaths in the early stages of the crisis.
summary_en: Did democracies handle the early COVID-19 pandemic better or worse than authoritarian states? Cepaluni, Dorsch and Branyiczki conduct a cross-country quantitative analysis of the first 100 days of the pandemic. Counterintuitively, more democratic countries experienced HIGHER per-capita COVID-19 deaths. The result is robust to controls, alternative estimation strategies, and instruments for political institutions. Policy responses in democracies were less effective at reducing early-stage deaths. The finding raises difficult questions about the relationship between democratic accountability and pandemic preparedness.
data_used: Cross-country panel of approximately 150 countries, first 100 days of COVID-19 pandemic (early 2020), with daily mortality data, V-Dem democracy indices, and policy-response measures from Oxford COVID-19 Government Response Tracker.
policy_relevance: Direct relevance for the Hungarian government's pandemic-preparedness review at NNK, the Pénzügyminisztérium, and the National Security Council. The paper provides a counterintuitive empirical finding that democratic governance is not automatically protective — useful framing for assessing institutional pandemic-readiness reforms.
title: Political regimes and deaths in the early stages of the COVID-19 pandemic
journal: Journal of Public Finance and Public Choice
